name: CERT-In — Cyber Security Directions (28 April 2022)
applies_to: Service providers, intermediaries, data centres, body corporates and government organisations (sector regulators cite these directions).

source.title: As applied by RBI NBFC Directions 2026 para 141 and SEBI CSCRF RS.CO.S1 ('within 6 hours of noticing/detecting')

obligations.label: Report the cyber incident to CERT-In

fields.label: Type of incident (e.g. ransomware, data breach, DDoS, unauthorised access)
Containment and recovery actions so far

obligations.notes: The 6-hour figure is confirmed by two regulator texts we hold; the reporting address and form come from CERT-In's site and must be confirmed there.

notes: CERT-In also expects ICT logs to be kept for 180 days within India and system clocks synchronised to NTP (NIC/NPL) - see the compliance maps.
